quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: To all staff: as announced in June, the company will relocate its head office to the Docklands building on Monday, 3 November. The move affects everyone in the finance, legal and marketing teams, who will occupy floors four to six. Removal crews will pack desks over the weekend, so please clear your drawers and label any personal items by Friday afternoon. IT will transfer your computer, but you must back up important files to the shared drive in advance. Parking at the new site is limited to sixty spaces, allocated by a lottery; those who miss out can apply for a discounted public transport pass, which will cover the cost of a monthly ticket. The nearest station, Quay Road, is a seven-minute walk from the entrance. A drop-in session on the new building will be held in the canteen on Thursday at 12:30, when questions can be raised with the facilities manager.
quests.question: How can staff who do not win a parking space be helped?
options: They will be moved to the third floor instead
They can use the sixty spaces on Thursdays only
They must ask IT to transfer their parking permit to the new site
They can apply for a transport pass covering a monthly ticket
quests.correctAnswer: They can apply for a transport pass covering a monthly ticket
quests.hint: Find the sentence where a limited resource is shared out, and read what happens to the unlucky ones.
quests.explanation: Parking is allocated by lottery, and those who miss out can apply for a discounted pass paying for a monthly ticket. The drop-in session is for questions, not parking.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Urban planners have been talking about the "fifteen-minute city", an idea that daily needs such as shops, schools, doctors and parks should be reachable within a quarter of an hour on foot or by bicycle. Supporters argue that this would reduce car use, strengthen local businesses and make neighbourhoods more sociable. Critics, however, fear that the plan could restrict where people are allowed to travel, although its designers insist that nobody would be prevented from leaving their district. In practice, the concept is closer to a design principle than to a rule: some cities, such as Paris and Melbourne, have adapted it by adding cycle lanes, converting parking spaces into public squares and encouraging services to open in local centres. The results so far are promising, but experts warn that the approach works best when accompanied by affordable housing, so that shops and schools nearby do not simply push up rents.
quests.question: Which statement best reflects the experts' warning?
options: Local improvements can raise housing costs unless homes stay affordable
Paris and Melbourne have already abandoned the idea
The plan forbids travel outside a person's own district
Cycle lanes are unnecessary in most neighbourhoods
quests.correctAnswer: Local improvements can raise housing costs unless homes stay affordable
quests.hint: The warning is introduced near the end by a verb such as "warn". Read what it depends on.
quests.explanation: Experts say the approach works best with affordable housing, so that nearby amenities do not push rents up. The fear about restricted travel is the critics' concern, and designers reject it.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Your electricity supplier is replacing old meters with smart meters, and an appointment has been arranged for your home on Wednesday between 8:00 a.m. and 12:00. The installation takes about an hour, during which the power will be off for around thirty minutes. Please make sure the engineer can reach the meter, which may be in a cupboard or garage, and that someone aged eighteen or over is present. Smart meters send your usage to us automatically, so you will no longer need to take readings, and your bills will be based on actual consumption, not estimates. You can also see your usage on a small display, which many customers use to identify appliances that use a lot of power. If you cannot attend, please call the number below at least two days in advance, or the missed appointment fee of twenty-five dollars may apply.
quests.question: What is the main advantage of a smart meter mentioned?
options: Readings can be taken by the customer more easily
The power stays on during installation
The fee for a missed appointment is removed
Bills reflect actual use, not estimates
quests.correctAnswer: Bills reflect actual use, not estimates
quests.hint: Look for the sentence that starts with what smart meters do and follow its consequences.
quests.explanation: Because usage is sent automatically, bills are based on real consumption. The power is briefly off during installation, and the missed-appointment fee is unrelated.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: A year ago I quit my office job to translate full time, and people keep asking whether I regret it. The honest answer is that the first six months were terrifying. I had savings but no clients, and I spent most mornings writing polite emails to agencies that never replied. Then a small publisher asked me to translate a cookbook, and the recommendation that followed brought two more commissions. Now I work a comfortable four days a week, although income still varies dramatically from month to month. The biggest surprise has been how much of the work is not translating at all: invoices, negotiation and learning to say no to projects that pay too little. If you are thinking of trying the same, my advice is to save at least half a year of expenses first and to keep your old contacts warm.
quests.question: What is the writer's main advice to people considering freelancing?
options: Accept every project, however low the pay
Build up savings and maintain former contacts
Work five days a week from the start
Avoid agencies and work with publishers
quests.correctAnswer: Build up savings and maintain former contacts
quests.hint: Advice usually comes at the very end and begins with a phrase like "my advice is".
quests.explanation: The final sentence recommends saving six months of expenses and keeping old contacts. Saying no to poorly paid projects is mentioned as a lesson, not accepting everything.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Scientists measuring the Kelvin Glacier report that its front has retreated by almost four kilometres since 1990, with about half of that loss occurring in the last decade. The team used satellite images, aerial photographs and, for the most recent years, drones that produce detailed three-dimensional maps. The rate of melting seems to have accelerated because warmer seawater is reaching the base of the glacier, weakening the ice from below. Local guides, who have taken visitors onto the glacier for forty years, say they can see the change in a single season: routes that were safe in one summer are crossed by deep cracks the next. Researchers stress that the glacier will not vanish soon, but the meltwater is already raising river levels downstream, which affects farmers and hydroelectric stations.
quests.question: According to the passage, why has melting accelerated?
options: Visitors have crossed the glacier more often
Farmers have diverted the rivers downstream
Warmer seawater is weakening the ice from below
Drones have damaged the surface
quests.correctAnswer: Warmer seawater is weakening the ice from below
quests.hint: The cause is named in a "because" clause in the third sentence.
quests.explanation: Warm seawater reaching the base weakens the glacier from underneath. Drones and satellites are measuring tools, not causes.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Old phones, cables and small appliances can be recycled at any of our stores, free of charge, whether or not you bought them from us. Simply place items in the yellow bin beside the customer service desk. Please remove batteries from toys and torches if you can, and take out any memory cards or SIM cards, as we cannot be responsible for personal data. Items containing lithium batteries, such as e-cigarettes, cannot be placed in the bin and must be handed to a member of staff. We accept up to five items per visit. Everything collected is sent to a specialist facility, where valuable metals are recovered and hazardous substances are removed safely. Last year, customers helped us collect more than sixty tonnes, which is equivalent to about a million phones.
quests.question: What should customers do with an e-cigarette?
options: Remove the battery and keep it
Put it in the yellow bin
Give it directly to a member of staff
Take it to a specialist facility
quests.correctAnswer: Give it directly to a member of staff
quests.hint: Find the exception to the rule about the yellow bin.
quests.explanation: Products with lithium batteries cannot go in the bin and must be handed to staff. The specialist facility is where the store sends the collected items.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Hi Paolo, following up on our discussion about the quarterly review call. The difficulty is finding a time that works across three time zones. Kim in Singapore can only join before 9 a.m. her time, which is 2 a.m. for you in Rome and 8 p.m. the previous evening for Jordan in Chicago. Jordan has suggested Thursday at 9 a.m. Chicago time, which would be 4 p.m. for you and midnight for Kim. Neither is ideal. My proposal is that we split the difference: hold the call at 7 a.m. Chicago time, which is 2 p.m. in Rome and 8 p.m. in Singapore, and ask everyone to prepare notes in advance so that the meeting can be kept to forty minutes. Could you let me know by tomorrow if that suits you, so I can send the invitation? Thanks, Alina
quests.question: What is Alina's proposal?
options: Two separate calls for different regions on different days
A shorter call at a time inconvenient for nobody in particular
A morning call in Singapore before nine
A written report instead of any call at all
quests.correctAnswer: A shorter call at a time inconvenient for nobody in particular
quests.hint: The proposal follows the words "My proposal is". Check whom the time inconveniences most.
quests.explanation: Seven a.m. in Chicago is mid-afternoon in Rome and evening in Singapore, a compromise for all three. She adds a forty-minute limit and advance notes.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: By the early 1980s, fewer than a thousand people spoke Hawaiian fluently, and almost no children did. Generations of pressure to use English in schools had almost erased it. In the 1980s, a small group of teachers and parents founded immersion preschools, where children were taught entirely in Hawaiian. The idea spread to primary and secondary schools, and in time a university programme trained new teachers. Today, tens of thousands of people speak Hawaiian at some level, and it is an official language of the state. The revival was not easy: materials had to be created, and older speakers were invited to work with young families. Linguists often cite the project as evidence that a language in serious decline can be revived if communities commit to teaching it to children.
quests.question: What made the revival possible, according to the passage?
options: A law that forced everyone to speak Hawaiian
Immersion schooling started by teachers and parents
Government support for English lessons
Textbooks brought from other countries
quests.correctAnswer: Immersion schooling started by teachers and parents
quests.hint: The important initiative is described in the sentence starting "In the 1980s".
quests.explanation: Parents and teachers founded immersion preschools, which then expanded. The passage does not mention any law forcing speakers, and English pressure caused the decline.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: After three months of using the Ridgeback electric bike for a twelve-kilometre commute, I can report that it has replaced my car on most days. The motor assists up to twenty-five kilometres an hour and is smooth rather than jerky, so I arrive without needing a shower. The battery, which lasts about sixty kilometres in mixed conditions, takes four hours to charge. On the downside, the bike weighs twenty-four kilograms, which makes it awkward to carry upstairs, and the supplied mudguards rattle on rough roads. The display is easy to read even in sunlight. The price, at $2,100, is significant, but I have calculated that the savings on fuel and parking will repay it in about three years. I would recommend it to anyone with a similar commute, although the weight might discourage those living in flats without a lift.
quests.question: For whom might the bike be less suitable?
options: People with a twelve-kilometre commute
People who commute in sunlight
People who dislike jerky motors
People living upstairs without a lift
quests.correctAnswer: People living upstairs without a lift
quests.hint: Find the drawback, then ask who would be most affected by it.
quests.explanation: The bike is heavy, and the writer notes it would discourage flat-dwellers without a lift. The commute distance and the display are positives.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Schools collect large amounts of information about pupils, including grades, attendance and, increasingly, data from learning apps. Under the new guidelines, each school must appoint a data protection officer, who will be responsible for making sure that information is stored securely and used only for educational purposes. Parents have the right to see what is held about their child and to ask for errors to be corrected. Schools may share data with outside companies only when a written agreement is in place, and pupils' photographs may not be published without consent. Any breach, such as the loss of a laptop containing records, must be reported within seventy-two hours. The guidelines also recommend that data no longer needed, for example the records of pupils who left five years ago, be deleted regularly. Inspectors will check compliance during their next round of visits.
quests.question: What must happen when a laptop with pupil records is lost?
options: Parents must be told before the school is informed
The officer must publish a photograph of the laptop
The breach must be reported within seventy-two hours
The data must be deleted after five years
quests.correctAnswer: The breach must be reported within seventy-two hours
quests.hint: The guidelines contain a deadline for reporting problems. Find the noun describing the problem.
quests.explanation: Any breach, including a lost laptop, must be reported within seventy-two hours. Deleting old records is a separate recommendation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Every Saturday morning, Dmitri Volkov teaches chess to a dozen children in a room above a bakery. He does not begin with strategy. Instead, he asks them to play a game with only kings and pawns, so that they learn to think about space and time before they learn how each piece moves. Parents say the effect goes beyond the board: children who found it hard to sit still now concentrate for an hour. Dmitri, who was once a national junior champion, laughs at this. "Chess doesn't make you clever," he says. "It makes you notice that you make the same mistake twice." He insists that losing is essential and that a child who never loses is not learning. He has never charged a fee, and the bakery provides tea and biscuits.
quests.question: What does Dmitri mean by his remark about mistakes?
options: Chess helps players become aware of their own repeated errors
Children should avoid losing games at all costs
Mistakes are impossible for good players in chess
Chess makes players cleverer than other children in school
quests.correctAnswer: Chess helps players become aware of their own repeated errors
quests.hint: Consider the attitude behind his laughing reply to the parents' claim.
quests.explanation: He rejects the idea that chess makes you clever and points instead to noticing recurring mistakes. He then adds that losing is important.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: When you use someone else's ideas in an essay, you must say where they came from. This is called citation, and it serves two purposes: it gives credit to the original author, and it allows readers to check your sources. There are several styles, but all require the same basic information, such as the author's name, the year and the title. Direct quotations must appear in quotation marks, with the page number, and should be used sparingly; in most cases, you should paraphrase, putting the idea in your own words while still citing the source. Merely changing a few words in a sentence is not enough, and may be considered plagiarism. If you are uncertain, it is better to cite than not to cite. Your tutor can tell you which style your department prefers.
quests.question: What is true of paraphrasing according to the guidance?
options: It is more common than quoting in every case
It removes the need to name the author
It still requires a citation
It means changing a few words
quests.correctAnswer: It still requires a citation
quests.hint: Test each option against the sentence about putting ideas in your own words.
quests.explanation: Paraphrasing means using your own words but still citing the source. Merely changing a few words is warned against as potential plagiarism.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The dredging of the harbour channel, planned to finish in March, will now continue until at least June. The port authority explains that surveyors found more silt than expected and that two of its three dredgers were out of action for repairs during the winter. As a result, ships larger than 200 metres have been diverted to a neighbouring port, and shipping agents estimate that the extra costs have already reached a million dollars. Local businesses that depend on the port, such as chandlers and tugboat operators, say they have lost income, although the authority points out that smaller vessels are unaffected. It has promised weekly updates and says that a fourth dredger will be hired next month. Environmental groups have asked that the dredged material be tested before being dumped at sea.
quests.question: Which ships have been affected by the delay?
options: Those longer than 200 metres
Vessels needing repairs
Only tugboats and chandlers
All ships using the harbour
quests.correctAnswer: Those longer than 200 metres
quests.hint: Notice which category the port authority says is spared.
quests.explanation: Ships over 200 metres are diverted, while smaller vessels are unaffected. Chandlers and tugboat operators lose income indirectly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Boredom has a poor reputation. We treat it as something to escape, and a phone is always at hand for the purpose. Yet psychologists have found that boredom can be productive. In one study, people who were made to do a dull task, such as copying phone numbers, then performed better on a creative test than those who had not been bored. The explanation may be that a wandering mind links ideas that would otherwise stay separate. Similarly, many writers and scientists report that their best ideas arrive during a walk, a shower or a long train journey, when nothing demands their attention. None of this means we should seek tedium deliberately. But it suggests that constant stimulation might crowd out the empty moments in which new thoughts form, and that a few minutes of doing nothing could be a useful habit.
quests.question: What point does the writer make about boredom?
options: People should seek out tedious work
Phones are harmful to everyone
Copying phone numbers improves memory
Moments of boredom can support creativity
quests.correctAnswer: Moments of boredom can support creativity
quests.hint: Ask what the study and the writers' reports are both used to demonstrate.
quests.explanation: Both the experiment and the anecdotes suggest that unstimulated time helps ideas link up. The writer explicitly says we should not seek tedium deliberately.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Comparing energy tariffs can save a typical household several hundred dollars a year, yet many customers never switch. There are three main types. A standard variable tariff changes with the supplier's costs and is usually the most expensive. A fixed tariff guarantees your price for a set period, usually one or two years, which makes budgeting easier but can leave you paying more if wholesale prices fall. Some fixed deals charge an exit fee if you leave early. A tracker tariff follows the wholesale market and can be cheaper, though bills may rise sharply in winter. When comparing, look at the unit price and the daily standing charge together, since a low unit price can be offset by a high standing charge, especially for people who use little energy.
quests.question: Why might a low unit price be misleading?
options: Exit fees are added to each unit of energy
Wholesale prices always fall in the winter months
Trackers never rise in price during winter
A high daily charge can cancel the saving
quests.correctAnswer: A high daily charge can cancel the saving
quests.hint: The answer involves two prices that must be viewed together.
quests.explanation: The daily standing charge can offset a low unit price, particularly for low users. The passage says trackers can rise sharply in winter.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: In 2019, a hospital in the north of the country noticed that infections among surgical patients were higher than at similar hospitals. Managers assumed the cause was equipment, and spent months upgrading sterilisation machines, without effect. Then a nurse suggested watching what actually happened on the ward. Observers discovered that staff were washing their hands correctly before operations but not always between patients on the ward, mainly because sinks were located far from beds. The hospital installed dispensers at every bedside and asked patients to remind staff politely. Within a year, infection rates dropped by a third. The case is now taught in medical schools as an example of how solutions often lie in observing behaviour, rather than in assuming the problem is technical.
quests.question: What was the actual cause of the higher infection rate?
options: Hand washing between patients was inconsistent
The sterilisation machines were faulty
Nurses washed their hands before operations only
Patients forgot to ask for help
quests.correctAnswer: Hand washing between patients was inconsistent
quests.hint: Compare the managers' first assumption with what the observers found.
quests.explanation: The staff washed properly before surgery but not always on the ward, partly because sinks were far from beds. Upgrading machines had no effect.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The island of Skarn is reached by ferry from the mainland port, a crossing of ninety minutes. In summer, there are four sailings a day, at 7:30, 11:00, 15:30 and 19:00, with the last return leaving the island at 20:15. In winter, the timetable is reduced to two sailings, at 9:00 and 16:00, and services are frequently cancelled because of high winds. Foot passengers do not need to book, but cars must be reserved at least forty-eight hours in advance, since only thirty vehicles can be carried. Bicycles travel free. There is a small shop and a cafe in the harbour, but no bank, so visitors are advised to bring cash. Several guesthouses are open all year, though they fill quickly in July and August.
quests.question: What is required to bring a car to the island?
options: A reservation at least two days ahead
Payment in cash at the harbour before boarding
A sailing in the summer timetable only
A guesthouse booking on the island for the night
quests.correctAnswer: A reservation at least two days ahead
quests.hint: One category of passenger has a condition that others do not.
quests.explanation: Cars must be reserved forty-eight hours in advance because of limited space. Foot passengers and bicycles can simply turn up.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: We are pleased to announce that Harlan Foods will merge with Brightfield Dairy, creating one of the region's largest food producers. The combined company will keep the Harlan name, and both current chief executives will remain in their posts for at least a year. Management stresses that no factory will close, and that the aim is to combine purchasing, share distribution networks and expand exports. Around forty administrative roles are expected to be affected, but affected staff will be offered retraining or voluntary redundancy terms. Shareholders will vote on the merger in November, and regulators must also approve it, which may take up to six months. Until the deal is complete, both companies will continue to operate independently, and customers should notice no changes.
quests.question: What must happen before the merger is complete?
options: A factory must close before the vote
Both chief executives must leave their posts within a year
Shareholders must vote and regulators must approve
Customers must sign new contracts with the company
quests.correctAnswer: Shareholders must vote and regulators must approve
quests.hint: A merger passes through two kinds of approval. Find both.
quests.explanation: The vote in November and regulatory approval are the conditions. The chief executives stay for at least a year, and no factory is closing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: When the last shop in Little Marston closed in 2016, residents faced a nine-kilometre trip to buy a loaf of bread. A public meeting produced an unusual idea: buy the building and run it themselves. Two hundred and eighty villagers invested between fifty and a thousand dollars each, and a local builder gave his time to convert the old chapel into a shop. It opened with a manager on a modest salary and a team of volunteers who work two-hour shifts. Prices are slightly higher than in supermarkets, but many people pay the difference, saying they would rather support something that belongs to the village. The shop also hosts a weekly coffee morning, which some older residents describe as the highlight of their week. Last year it made a small profit, which will be used to install a post office counter.
quests.question: Why do people accept slightly higher prices in the shop?
options: The chapel is a historic building
The shop offers better quality than supermarkets
The manager's salary is high
They value supporting a community-owned business
quests.correctAnswer: They value supporting a community-owned business
quests.hint: Look for what shoppers say they prefer, rather than what the prices are.
quests.explanation: Villagers say they would rather support something that belongs to them. Quality is not compared, and the manager's salary is described as modest.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: A mortgage is a loan used to buy a home, with the property itself serving as security. Lenders usually require a deposit, often ten to twenty percent of the price, and the rest is borrowed and repaid, with interest, over a term of twenty-five years or more. In the early years, most of each payment covers interest, and only a small part reduces the debt. A fixed rate keeps payments the same for a set period, typically two to five years, after which the loan moves to the lender's standard rate, which is usually higher. Borrowers who do not want a sudden rise often remortgage, switching to a new deal before the fixed period ends. If payments are missed for a long time, the lender can eventually take possession of the property.
quests.question: Why do many borrowers remortgage?
options: To reduce the deposit they had paid at the start
To avoid a jump in payments when the fixed rate ends
To move to a different property before the term ends
To repay all the interest before the principal
quests.correctAnswer: To avoid a jump in payments when the fixed rate ends
quests.hint: The reason follows the phrase "who do not want".
quests.explanation: When a fixed period ends, payments usually jump to the standard rate, so borrowers switch beforehand. The deposit is paid at purchase and is unrelated.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dear participants, I am sorry to tell you that Saturday's pottery workshop has been cancelled. Our instructor, Ms. Delacroix, fell ill on Thursday and her doctor has advised her to rest for at least ten days. We considered finding a replacement, but the technique she teaches requires specialist kilns that only she is trained to operate. Everyone who paid will receive a full refund within five working days, and those who prefer can transfer their place to the next workshop on 21 June, which has some spare capacity. Please tell us by Wednesday which you prefer; if we do not hear from you, we will issue the refund automatically. We know many of you travelled some distance to attend, and we are grateful for your understanding. Kind regards, Joy Bello
quests.question: Why was no substitute instructor found?
options: The workshop was fully booked
The doctor forbade replacements
Only Ms. Delacroix could operate the kilns
All other instructors were on holiday
quests.correctAnswer: Only Ms. Delacroix could operate the kilns
quests.hint: The organiser explains her reason directly after mentioning a replacement.
quests.explanation: The technique needs specialist kilns and only Ms. Delacroix is trained for them. Refund and transfer options are separate.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: In autumn, the leaves of many trees turn red, orange and yellow before falling. The green colour comes from chlorophyll, which absorbs sunlight to make food. As days shorten and temperatures drop, the tree stops producing chlorophyll, and the green fades. The yellow and orange pigments, which were present all along, are now visible. Red is different: it comes from anthocyanins, which are produced in the leaf in autumn, especially when days are bright and nights are cool. This is why some years produce more spectacular displays than others. Scientists are still debating why trees make red pigment at all, since the leaves are about to fall. One theory suggests that it acts as a sunscreen, protecting the leaf while the tree recovers valuable nutrients from it.
quests.question: What is the difference between the red and the yellow colours?
options: Red pigments come from chlorophyll that stays in the leaf
Yellow pigments are always present, while red pigments are newly made
Yellow pigments appear only when nights are cool
Red leaves have stopped absorbing sunlight entirely
quests.correctAnswer: Yellow pigments are always present, while red pigments are newly made
quests.hint: The passage contrasts the origin of the colours with the words "Red is different".
quests.explanation: Yellow and orange were hidden by green, while red is produced in the leaf in autumn. Chlorophyll gives the green.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The customer satisfaction survey, completed by 2,400 people, shows an overall score of 81 percent, up from 76 last year. Customers were most positive about staff helpfulness, at 92 percent, and least positive about waiting times, where only 58 percent were satisfied. Delivery speed improved most, rising eleven points after the opening of the second warehouse. Interestingly, satisfaction was lowest among customers who had contacted the helpline, at 63 percent, suggesting that problems were not resolved on the first call. Management has therefore set two priorities for the coming year: reducing waiting times at the returns desk and training helpline staff to solve queries without transferring calls. Comments from customers will be shared with each team, and the survey will be repeated in March.
quests.question: What does the low score among helpline users suggest?
options: The warehouse was too far away from the customers
Staff were unhelpful in shops and at the returns desk
The helpline was too expensive for most customers
Problems were often not solved in the first call
quests.correctAnswer: Problems were often not solved in the first call
quests.hint: Read the sentence after the figure; the writer draws a conclusion from it.
quests.explanation: The survey writer infers that the low score reflects unresolved problems on the first call. That is why helpline training is a priority.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: I am delighted to recommend Ms. Ayaka Mori for the position of project manager. I have worked with her for six years, during which she led the redesign of our ordering system, a project that many colleagues considered impossible within the budget. She achieved it by listening carefully to staff who used the old system and by breaking the work into stages that could be tested. Ayaka is calm under pressure and has an unusual ability to explain technical problems in simple terms. If she has a weakness, it is that she takes on too much herself rather than delegating; she is aware of this and has been working on it. I believe she would be an asset to any organisation. Please contact me if you need more information. Yours faithfully, David Ruiz
quests.question: What weakness does the writer mention?
options: She is anxious under pressure
She tends to do too much herself
She ignores staff opinions
She explains problems poorly
quests.correctAnswer: She tends to do too much herself
quests.hint: A letter of recommendation places any criticism carefully; look for a conditional phrase.
quests.explanation: The only weakness is taking on too much rather than delegating, and the writer says she is working on it. The other options contradict praise elsewhere.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: A decade ago, most European night trains were being cut, replaced by cheap flights. Now the service is returning. Several countries have introduced new sleeper routes, and passengers report that the idea of arriving in a city centre after a night of sleep has fresh appeal. Concerns about flying's emissions have helped, but so has practical convenience: a night train saves a hotel bill and avoids airport queues. Operators still face problems. The carriages are expensive to build, and tracks are shared with freight, which leads to delays. Ticket prices can also be high, since a sleeper compartment is more costly to run than a seat. Nevertheless, bookings for many routes are full months ahead, and companies are ordering more carriages. Whether the revival lasts will depend on governments continuing to support cross-border timetables.
quests.question: What will determine whether the revival lasts?
options: The price of flights compared with sleeper tickets
Continued government support for cross-border services
The number of hotel rooms available in city centres
The length of freight trains sharing the same tracks
quests.correctAnswer: Continued government support for cross-border services
quests.hint: The final sentence states what the outcome depends on.
quests.explanation: The passage ends by saying the revival depends on governments supporting cross-border timetables. Flights and hotels are mentioned only as background.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Losing files is easy and painful. Hard drives fail, phones are lost and laptops are stolen, so a backup should be part of any routine. Experts recommend the "three-two-one" rule: keep three copies of anything important, on two different types of storage, with one copy kept in a different location. For most people, this means the original on the computer, a copy on an external drive and a third stored online. External drives should be checked every few months, since they can fail silently. Cloud storage is convenient because it works automatically, but read the terms carefully: some services delete files if an account is inactive for a long time. Whichever method you choose, test your backup by restoring a file, because a backup you have never tested is only a hope.
quests.question: Why does the writer advise testing a backup?
options: Testing makes the files smaller
External drives cost more than laptops
An untested backup may not work when needed
Cloud services delete files each month
quests.correctAnswer: An untested backup may not work when needed
quests.hint: The final clause states the writer's view with a striking comparison.
quests.explanation: Calling an untested backup "only a hope" means you cannot be sure it works. The cloud warning concerns long inactivity, not monthly deletion.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Potholes form when water seeps into cracks in the road surface, freezes and expands, breaking the asphalt. Traffic then loosens the pieces, and a small crack becomes a hole within days. Councils say that repairing them is a losing battle: a pothole patched in February may reopen by April because temporary repairs are cheap and short-lived. Drivers, meanwhile, pay a heavy price, with the cost of damaged tyres and suspension estimated at hundreds of millions each year. This newspaper believes that the current approach is wrong. Filling holes one by one is like mopping the floor while the tap runs. Roads should be resurfaced properly, which costs more at the start but far less over ten years. It is time for the council to invest in prevention rather than quick fixes.
quests.question: What is the writer's opinion?
options: Roads should be properly resurfaced instead of patched
Potholes are unavoidable in winter and cannot be prevented
Drivers should pay directly for pothole repairs
Councils are repairing potholes too slowly each spring
quests.correctAnswer: Roads should be properly resurfaced instead of patched
quests.hint: Identify what the comparison with the tap is criticising, then read the last two sentences.
quests.explanation: The editorial says that patching is like mopping while the tap runs and calls for lasting resurfacing. The focus is on method, not on speed.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Research by a transport consultancy suggests that people underestimate how much time they spend looking for parking. In a survey of 3,000 drivers in five cities, the average driver reported spending about four minutes per trip searching for a space, but when researchers used tracking data, the actual figure was nearly ten. The difference was largest in city centres, where drivers circle blocks hoping for a cheaper space near their destination instead of paying for a car park. This behaviour, the authors argue, adds significantly to congestion: in one district, nearly a third of traffic at peak times was made up of cars looking for somewhere to stop. They recommend that cities set parking prices according to demand, so that a few spaces on each street are always free, and that they publish real-time information on availability.
quests.question: Why do drivers circle blocks, according to the research?
options: They are following tracking apps
They underestimate the time they spend searching
They hope to find a cheaper space near their destination
They cannot find any car parks
quests.correctAnswer: They hope to find a cheaper space near their destination
quests.hint: A behaviour and its motive are linked in a single sentence about city centres.
quests.explanation: Drivers circle for cheaper spaces close to where they are going instead of paying for a car park. The underestimate of time is a separate finding.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: When the department store Hartley's announced that it would close its flagship building after 140 years, reaction was emotional. Shoppers remembered Christmas windows, the tea room on the fifth floor and the lift attendants in uniform. Yet the reasons were less sentimental. Sales in the building had fallen for a decade as shoppers moved online, and the cost of heating and maintaining seven floors had become unsustainable. The company plans to sell the building and open smaller shops in three shopping centres, and to expand its website, which already accounts for a third of turnover. Some former staff feel that the decision was inevitable, but others believe the store could have survived by renting out unused floors. A local group is now campaigning for the building to be turned into a market hall.
quests.question: What does the word "Yet" signal in the passage?
options: A move from emotional reactions to practical reasons
A prediction about the future of the market hall
A criticism of online shopping and its effects
A denial that the store is closing after all
quests.correctAnswer: A move from emotional reactions to practical reasons
quests.hint: Ask which two kinds of explanation the writer is placing side by side.
quests.explanation: "Yet" shifts from nostalgic reactions to the financial reasons for closure. It does not deny the closure or attack the internet.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dr. Farah Naseri has spent her career studying how children learn to read, and her latest study, following 600 pupils for six years, offers a reassuring message. Children who began school unable to recognise letters had caught up by age eight, provided they received regular help. However, the study also found that home reading habits mattered more than any classroom method. Pupils whose families shared books, even for ten minutes a day, made faster progress than those whose parents worked long hours and had little chance to read with them. Dr. Naseri does not blame parents. Instead, she calls for schools to offer reading sessions in the early evening and for libraries to lend picture books to families who cannot afford to buy them. "Reading is not a talent," she says. "It is a habit that needs company."
quests.question: What does Dr. Naseri suggest should be done for busy families?
options: Provide reading opportunities through schools and libraries
Make classroom methods more difficult for children
Blame parents for not having enough time to read
Start school at an earlier age for all pupils
quests.correctAnswer: Provide reading opportunities through schools and libraries
quests.hint: A word of contrast after "does not blame parents" introduces her recommendation.
quests.explanation: She proposes early-evening sessions at schools and lending of picture books by libraries. She explicitly refuses to blame parents.
